name: Heathen Tribe Expansion and Evolution
description: New Believers. The Heathen camp lives and grows as a tribe of its own. **A growing camp makes The Last Heathen harder to reach, or impossible: that puzzle is solved only when no Heathen is left, and with births and new arrivals the camp may never empty.** Its Settings... button holds the two sliders and the options. AGING: every Heathen ages as believers do and can die of old age by the believers' rule -- the camp's Heathens, villagers who left your tribe and the puzzle Heathens. A puzzle Heathen whose puzzle is not solved yet is replaced at once in the same role, so every puzzle can still be solved. COUPLES AND BABIES: two adult Heathens who are not kin (never parent and child, full or half siblings) pair for life, until one dies or joins your tribe; a couple can be of either sex. A woman in a couple with a man has babies: at 1x about one baby for the whole tribe every 24 real-life hours on Normal speed (12 on Fast, 40 on Slow), with twins 5.25% and triplets 1.75% of the time ("0.1-10x Heathen Tribe Births"). Births go on after The Last Heathen while a Heathen woman and a Heathen man are alive. Island events may give any couple a baby. NEW ARRIVALS ("0-10x New Heathen Arrivals", 0 = none): at 1x one arrival about every 48 real-life hours on Normal -- one to four Heathens, sometimes a couple with up to two children -- before and after The Last Heathen. Newcomers and Heathen babies are mostly blue-masked: 90% blue, 7% orange, 3% red (all blue with the option). A NEW CHIEF AND MASTERS: when the Heathen Chief or a Heathen Master dies after their puzzle is solved, the eldest adult Heathen takes the role -- for show (the role's skills, mask and title) until The Last Heathen is solved, the real role after it; a regrown camp of six adults gets a Chief and Masters again. Every later Chief, Master, Doctor or Mommy can be of either sex. A show Chief who joins your tribe becomes a real Retired Chief. CHILDREN GROW UP: when one of the camp's own children reaches 14, a new child takes their place at once, in the same camp role and mask -- the Rascal, the camp's orange-masked child, is replaced by a new Rascal -- and the grown one stays as an adult (an Arrived record "Replaced a Heathen child who grew up"). Babies of Heathen couples, arrivals' children and children who left your tribe are the tribe's growth and are not replaced. After The Last Heathen this happens only while New Heathen Arrivals is above 0. ELDERS RETIRE: at the game's elder age (55, later with Medicine) a Heathen with a camp role or a puzzle role -- the Heathen Doctor, a Heathen Master, the Heathen Mommy -- retires to the encampment and the eldest younger adult Heathen takes the role, with the puzzle's own set-up (the Mommy's successor carries her infant), so every puzzle can still be solved. **The Heathen Chief never retires.** With nobody younger the elder keeps the role until someone grows up or arrives. Elder Heathens keep their walking pace; elder believers still slow down as in the game. SICKNESS AND HEATHEN DOCTORS: Heathens fall sick by the believers' rule; ordinary Heathens with Healing skill heal them (never the puzzle's Heathen Doctor); with nobody able they get well on their own. A sick Heathen never dies of it and never drops below 21 health. Heathens never eat from your food store and never starve. Heathen cures never count in People Cured. SHOW ACTIONS (about 1 in 4 of an idle adult Heathen's choices at the default 25%): harvesting noni, crops or fish once the puzzle that opens each to your believers is solved -- never taking anything, carried to the encampment, not the granary; visiting the pools, the Believer Idol, the science lab, the farm plots, and the Love Shack and Clothing Hut doors once built (no embrace, no clothes); a show meal; devotion at the mud hut. Heathens do only what believers of their age do: children play in the nursery while someone teaches there, and the Love Shack only at the couples' ages. None of it changes anything of your believers'. SKILLS grow by practice as believers' do, Devotion included (no tech bonus, no trophies); a Heathen keeps them on joining your tribe. THE SHRINE TO THE ANCESTORS: every Heathen who dies leaves a skeleton. Heathens carry their own dead to the mud hut and bury them there; believers do it, still to the mud hut, when no Heathen can (once The Buried Mausoleum is solved). Click the mud hut, or drop a villager on it, to see the Shrine to the Ancestors: the game's own Mausoleum screen with the Heathens' graves. A villager who left your tribe and died a Heathen goes there; one who rejoined your tribe goes to your Mausoleum. Heathen graves already in your Mausoleum stay there. Day of Honor, the Remembrance Ceremony and Honoring the dead count the Shrine's graves. ISLAND EVENTS: Heathens can be chosen for island events, the new ones and the game's own, and the Heathen-Exclusive Events can happen. A sick Heathen is never chosen; the puzzles' Heathens can be in a new event but nothing in it really happens to them ("(no effect)"); in the game's own events a Heathen's Faith never changes; outcomes for the whole tribe happen to the Heathens' village when only Heathens are in an event ("(no effect)"). LOGS: each Heathen's conception, birth, couple, arrival, new role, retirement, death and grave goes in the logs, marked as a Heathen. **Heathens never count in the Village Statistics.** Heathens always leave 10 villager records free. This row replaces "Heathen Tribe Ages, Dies and Has Children", "All Heathens Leave Skeletons" and "Heathens can be selected in Island Events/Heathen-Exclusive Events": a saved selection with any of them ticks this row. "Former Villagers Keep Aging Among the Heathens" and "Former Villagers Among the Heathens Leave Skeletons" stay separate (with this row on they change nothing more). Off by default and in Select All; Owner's Defaults ticks it, with new arrivals at 1x. **Needs Story / Cheat Upgrades for the island events and the show Chief's and Masters' titles; the Heathen-Exclusive Events also need the Isola Grand Event Collection.** **Not yet seen in a running game** (checked by emulation of the stock executable). The companions are "VVFP Heathen Aging.dll", "VVFP Heathen Life.dll" and "VVFP Heathen Mausoleum.dll"; they keep their own small files per save and never write a save.

needs_on.for: the island-event engine that chooses the villagers, and the show Chief's and Masters' titles

behavior_changes: The age credit 0x46FE90 adds a living aging Heathen's units to its age +0x1B8C, as 0x46F7F0 does for a believer (0x470077); every other Heathen as the stock game (no age).

The life tick 0x472C90 gives an aging Heathen one unit for each unit of its age not yet processed (+0x1C3C), live and in the load-time catch-up (through the age credit and the life tick), and after an Origins Time Warp or a Story / Cheat Upgrades time skip, which write the ages themselves and credit the Heathens this companion ages (VvfpHeathenAgingAges): at each whole year of the processed age past 1,100 + 160 x (Medicine - 1) units (the tech level read at 0x51D5D0, as 0x423600(1) reads it), rand(100) < 10 x the years over takes them -- the believers' old-age rule (0x472FC6..0x47304A). Nothing else of a believer's unit runs: no eating, starving, sickness, health, Faith drift, job or offline job ticks.

A death: with a skeleton row covering them, SetHealth 0x4758B0(0, 2 Old age) makes the body the believers' "Burying the dead" (0x46F130, 0x473F50) buries into the Roster of the Dead 0x464C70, as a believer's; the Village Statistics' death counter 0x51D3A0 is put back; a puzzle Heathen's body gets role 0 so the role finder 0x470690 finds the new one. Otherwise the activity stops (0x473440), the selection is dropped when it is theirs (0x4653D0, 0x470800), the presence byte +0x1CD4 is cleared, health untouched, and the Cause of Death companion writes the Death record (VvfpCauseDiedAmongHeathens: Old age, "no grave (died among the Heathens: nothing was left)"; "... the Isolans ..." with the Guardians of Isola Rewrite). Its replacement's Arrived record says "Replaced a Heathen who died of old age" or "... lost in an island event" ("Replaced an Isolan ..." with the Guardians of Isola Rewrite).

The replacement, in the same tick, by the Heathen creator 0x46FD20 (Faith 1 there, so its SetFaith never runs to-a-Heathen; the stock camp's Faith written to +0x1CF0 after: -38 - rand(30), or the dead one's own when it was one of the five easy blue Faiths -5, -9, -16, -23, -30 of 0x470E60): an ordinary Heathen in the dead one's camp role (0..11) and mask (+0x1CED orange, +0x1CEE red), age 400, random sex; a former villager (no puzzle role) never replaced, and nobody once The Last Heathen (puzzle 25) is solved (the owner, 2026-11-23); a puzzle Heathen (roles 12-17) whose puzzle (1, 16, 13, 9, 5, 17: progress 0x51E008 + 8p against 0x51DF30 + 4p) is unsolved by the stock camp's own set-up of that role (0x424AC0; the Heathen Mommy's as the restored puzzle makes her, with her infant 0x465E00 forced, its father an adult Heathen man when there is one). A full table: owed until a record is free, kept in the slot's own file (each owed replacement with its role, masks and Faith), so a quit or a Change Tribe never loses or moves it; with no Heathen alive, or once The Last Heathen is solved, it is dropped. The Cause of Death companion writes its Arrived record (VvfpCauseHeathenArrived).

Who turned Heathen: a living Heathen the age credit last saw as that very believer (any path: the Faith drift, island events, The Spa, The Cracked Mask, a Custom Island Event; no call site spliced), by identity (name, likes, dislikes; carried to the new identity when the likes change in place or the name changes), kept per save slot in "Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <S>\Data\Heathen Aging\Heathen Aging - Save <S>.dat"; one who turned before the row by the parents on the record (+0x1BC0 / +0x1BD9).

"VVFP Heathen Aging.dll" with "VVFP Heathen Tribe Evolution.txt" (which stands for the folded rows' three flags; the old flags are still read): every Heathen ages and can die of old age by the believers' rule, a puzzle Heathen whose puzzle is unsolved is replaced at once by the stock camp's own set-up of that role, and every Heathen leaves a body for the burial.

Births: each aging Heathen woman 14-45, not expecting, not the Heathen Mommy, in a couple with a living adult Heathen man, rolls 1 in 2,400 x W / t a unit (W such women, t the births slider in tenths, 1..100; "VVFP Heathen Tribe Births.txt", 1x when missing): about one conception for the tribe every 240 units at 1x. Through 0x465E00 forced, her partner the father; the twins and triplets counters put back; the litter rolled by the companion: twins 5.25%, triplets 1.75%, capped by room. Births go on after The Last Heathen.

Couples (decision 15): two living adult Heathens of either sex, not kin (parent and child; full and half siblings, by the records' parent name, head and body), pair for life, at most one new couple a look; kept per slot in "Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <S>\Data\Heathen Couples\Heathen Couples - Save <S>.dat" ('VHC1'), following renames.  An unreadable couples file is never replaced, and pauses that village's couples, births and arrivals.

Arrivals: rolled once a unit of the village's clock, 1 in 4,800 / t (t the arrivals slider in tenths, 0..100; "VVFP Heathen Arrivals.txt", 0 = none when missing): a group of 1-4 (40/30/20/10%), half of the groups of two or more a couple with 0-2 children aged 2-12, made by the Heathen creator 0x46FD20 (Faith 1, then the camp's Faith written), roles 0-11, placed beside a living Heathen; never from nobody before The Last Heathen.

Masks of arrivals and newborns (decision 7): 90% blue, 7% orange, 3% red ("VVFP Heathen Options.txt" mask_orange_percent / mask_red_percent; 0 / 0 with "Keep every new Heathen blue"); the puzzle roles keep their own masks.

Roles (decision 6): a dead Chief or Master whose puzzle is solved is succeeded by the eldest adult ordinary Heathen -- the real role 13-16 after The Last Heathen, otherwise for show (the role's skills, the Chief's or the purple mask through the Origins mask store, the original's own title through Story / Cheat Upgrades' VvfpStorySetCustomTitle); a regrown camp of 6 adults gets a real Chief and Masters; a show Chief who converts is given role 13 (the Retired Chief) and the show title is taken off.

Children who grow up (the owner, 2026-11-26): when a camp child (a Heathen with no recorded parents, never a former villager; roles 0-11) reaches 280 units in the life tick, a new child is made at once by the Heathen creator 0x46FD20 in the same role and mask, Healing 0, the stock camp's Faith: the Rascal (the Details title 0x4430AE..0x4430D6, string 0xD2: a Heathen younger than 280 in the orange mask; the stock camp's 0x424D23, age 140) by a Rascal of 140, a blue child at 120 or 240 (0x424CF9, 0x424D4D); its Arrived record "Replaced a Heathen child who grew up" ("... an Isolan child ...").  No room (10 records kept free): owed in the slot's file.  After The Last Heathen only while New Heathen Arrivals is above 0.

Elders retire (the owner, 2026-11-26; "the chief shouldn't retire"): an elder by the game's test 0x46F790 (age >= 160 x Medicine + 840) who holds a camp role 1-11, a puzzle role 12, 14-17 while its puzzle is unsolved, or a Master's role for show or after The Last Heathen gives it, at a throttled look, to the eldest adult Heathen who is not an elder and holds none (for a puzzle role a camp-role holder when there is none), set up as the stock camp sets the role up (skill, Faith; the Mommy's infant by the game's forced conception with a named other parent) -- never the Chief (13); the elder's role becomes 0, the Heathen AI's default (0x46EAD9 -> 0x46F007, the camp wander at the encampment).  Nobody younger: no retirement.  Records "Retired to the encampment" (VvfpCauseHeathenRetired) and "Took the role" (VvfpCauseHeathenRole).

Elders keep their pace: at 0x4659C5 (the walk set-up 0x465980's `lea ecx, [esi+0x1B8C]; call 0x46F790`, the slow pace 0x28 for an elder at 0x465A06) a Heathen skips the elder test; a believer elder still slows.

Partners: the life tick's partner cache is checked against the couple's saved identities before every use, and a Heathen who leaves (a death, an island event) is dropped from it at once, so a reused record is never taken for a partner.
Room (decision 18 as changed): Heathens are made only while 10 villager records stay free, in every population mode and in the 256 build.

"VVFP Heathen Life.dll" (VvfpHeathenLifeUnit, called by Heathen Aging's life-tick splice): the believers' sickness onset 0x465F50 for ordinary Heathens, their damage never below the floor (21; options sick_floor) written straight to health (never a cause that can kill), their +1 recovery; Heathen doctors (the best Healing among ordinary adult Heathens, never role 12) judged by the believers' skill check; well on their own 1 in 240 a unit with no healer; skill practice by the believers' rule with no tech bonus and no trophies.

Show actions (the picker 0x46F0BA, on options show_percent of an idle ordinary adult's picks; 25 by default): the game's own step adders with the skill-check and payoff steps left out -- noni, crops (the farm plots) and fish once their puzzles (2, 5, 10) are solved, carried to the encampment; the pools, the Believer Idol once carved, the science lab, the Love Shack (the couples' ages, no embrace) and the Clothing Hut (no clothes) doors once built; a show meal (no food taken); devotion at the mud hut; a child's nursery play while someone teaches at the nursery school.
People Cured: the drag-a-healer cure's +1 is skipped for a Heathen patient (the Village Statistics row's own technique; with that row applied its detours are left alone).

Logs: every forced Heathen conception gets its Conception record (WriteParentageRecordWithFather); a couple a "Couple formed" record (WriteParentageHeathenCouple); a new arrival an Arrived record "Arrived at the Heathen camp" or "... with N other(s)" ("Isolan" with Guardians of Isola Rewrite; VvfpCauseHeathenArrived); a new Chief or Master a "Took the role" record (VvfpCauseHeathenRole); each marked "Faction: Heathen".

"VVFP Heathen Mausoleum.dll" (the Shrine to the Ancestors): a Heathen's grave -- decided by the faction at death: a camp Heathen, an arrival, a puzzle Heathen or a former villager who died a Heathen -- goes to a table of its own laid out as the game's Roster of the Dead (500 graves), written by the game's own writer, so its epitaph, cause and job are the game's.  A believer's grave, a converted former villager's included, goes to the Roster of the Dead as before.  A full table: no grave, the body gone, the Death record says so.

Heathens bury Heathens (decision 11): an able adult Heathen starts the game's own "Burying the dead" on a Heathen's body and carries it to the mud hut; believers bury it (once The Buried Mausoleum is solved) only when no Heathen can or it has lain 120 units, still to the mud hut.

The mud hut (hotspot 0x0B, registered and stamped after each map load) opens the game's own Mausoleum screen on the Shrine's table with a click or a villager dropped on it, once it holds a grave; the title says "Shrine to the Ancestors" (translatable), the art is the game's own.  Holding a villager over it shows "<name> sees a heartfelt memorial shrine." (Fix Vanilla Bugs' hovel hover line).

The table is kept per save slot in "Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher\Save <S>\Data\Heathen Mausoleum\Heathen Mausoleum - Save <S>.dat" ('VHM1'), written only when the game saves the slot and read when it loads it; a new village clears it; Start Over forgets it (VVFP Save Reset.dll).

Day of Honor, the everyday Honoring the dead, the Remembrance Ceremony and Story / Cheat Upgrades' "graves" condition count the Shrine's graves too; the Village Statistics never do.  The Deaths log names the grave "the Shrine to the Ancestors (...)", or "no grave (the Shrine to the Ancestors was full)".

Story / Cheat Upgrades casts a Heathen (faction set, never sick, health above 0) in a new event's role marked "heathens": "allowed", "kin" or "only" while this row is installed; a role marked "only" takes no believer, and without this row nobody, so its event is not offered.  Every villager role of the existing added events New Believers shows is "allowed" or "kin" (data/event_collection/heathen_roles_existing.json, from the owner's approved audit), and the Living Event Engine's and the procedural events' roles are "allowed".
A "kin" role (a family role: a kinship relation, a pregnancy's other parent) and its family are one faction: a Heathen only beside Heathen family, a believer only beside believers.

A puzzle's Heathen (roles 12-17) may be cast in a new event, and nothing is ever made to them: every effect naming them is told, never made (their record is only read), and the page says "Nothing really happens to <name>. (no effect)"; the Island Events log has nothing of theirs.

A cast Heathen's "believer" words are swapped automatically: "(friend), a believer," / "(name1) is a believer" / a role called "believer" (and Guardians of Isola's "a villager of faith") become "a person of faith".

The game's own island events (Story / Cheat Upgrades, story_heathen_stock.inc): every believer part may draw an ordinary Heathen in proportion (the picker 0x471870 called again for Heathens: never roles 12-17, never sick); a Heathen part never takes the same Heathen; The Vision, The Mask, Doubt, The Spa and The Cracked Mask never change a drawn Heathen's Faith or faction (their Faith is kept below 0 around the apply and put back); the group events Isola Day Celebration, Blessings Day Celebration, Day of Honor, The Especially Offensive Cloud, The Bottle of Spicy Juice, Mushroom Day!, The Bed Bugs and Innovation in Farming also start their behaviour on the ordinary Heathens (The Allergy Season and The Salty Air already do, through the game's 0x470D60).

When every villager cast is a Heathen, the event's food, tech points, award, building damage or repair, goods, trades, tech level and whole-village effects are made nowhere: each automatic line says it happens to the Heathens' village (the Isolans' village with Guardians of Isola Rewrite) and ends "(no effect)".

An event's death or disappearance of a cast Heathen goes through "VVFP Heathen Aging.dll" (VvfpHeathenAgingEventGone): a body only with a skeleton row (the statistics' death counter put back), else the activity stopped, the presence byte cleared and a Death record (Cause of Death's VvfpCauseDiedAmongHeathens); then the replacement of a camp Heathen by the Heathen creator 0x46FD20, as for an old-age death.

An event's pregnancy of a cast Heathen goes through the same companion (VvfpHeathenAgingEventPregnancy): the game's conception 0x465E00 with a Heathen father only (the twins counters put back), the mother kept as expecting and aging until the companion's Heathen birth 40 units later (at once for a nursing baby); none once The Last Heathen is solved.
With this row "VVFP Heathen Aging.dll" splices its two sites even with no aging row ticked; then only a Heathen expecting an event's baby ages, until the birth.
More Island Events casts a Heathen only in a role its table names: The Aspiring Adventurer's adventurer and friend.

The Heathen-Exclusive Events HE-01..HE-45 (Isola Grand Event Collection, New Believers only; cie-v6-binary.md 47): "at least N graves" read from the game's own count (0x464E90 on 0x5481A8); the encampment's honoring and reflecting started through the hovel patch's own entries (0x494B83, 0x494DF1) when its bytes are in, else "Sitting"; a group of every ordinary Heathen (or N at random), never roles 12-17, never sick.
The Island Events log ends each Heathen's record with "Faction: Heathen" ("Isolan" with Guardians of Isola Rewrite).
explicit_non_changes: No executable byte is patched: the three companions splice their sites at run time, only after verifying their stock bytes, each all or none; Story / Cheat Upgrades splices the game's-own-event sites the same way.
Nothing is written to a save.  The companions keep their own files per save slot (Heathen Aging, Heathen Couples, Heathen Mausoleum), each written atomically and never replaced when unreadable.

Heathens never count in the Village Statistics: births, arrivals, cures, deaths and the Shrine's graves are all left out; Babies Made, People Cured, the twins and triplets counters and the death counter are put back or never touched.
Show actions never take from a source, the food store, a building, tech points or a believer's skill.
The puzzle Heathens (roles 12-17) keep their stock behaviour while their puzzles are unsolved.
The game's own island events' texts, choices and chances are never changed; only who may be drawn.
A Heathen never counts in the Village Statistics; nothing is ever made to a puzzle's Heathen.
